quizzes.title: Republic Day: History and Origins
quizzes.passage: Republic Day is celebrated in India on 26 January each year, and its origins lie in the freedom movement. This is the 77th Republic Day, marked in 2026. A session of the Indian National Congress passed a resolution that set out a clear political goal for the country. In the years that followed, Congress asked Indians to observe 26 January as a day of national pride, and the date was marked in this way for many years. The country later gained freedom, which led people to reconsider what the day should mean. The Constitution of India was then adopted by the Constituent Assembly, and it provided a new legal framework for the nation. The date chosen for the Constitution to take effect was 26 January, partly because of its nationalist significance. Because of this link, the day is closely associated with the Constitution. Celebrations begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas in honour of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose's birth anniversary. Today the main celebrations take place at Kartavya Path, formerly Rajpath, in New Delhi, where a parade is held. The celebrations conclude with the Beating Retreat ceremony at Vijay Chowk, and the day remains a reminder of the journey from colonial rule to a republic.

questions.q: Which demand was made by the resolution passed by the Indian National Congress in December 1929?
options: Dominion status within the British Commonwealth
Total self-rule, sovereignty and complete independence from British rule
Provincial autonomy under a new Government of India Act
Transfer of power to a central interim council
questions.explanation: The Poorna Swaraj resolution called for total self-rule, sovereignty and complete independence from British rule.

questions.q: Between 1930 and 1947, 26 January was celebrated in India as:
options: Independence Day or Poorna Swaraj Day
questions.explanation: From 1930 to 1947, 26 January was celebrated as Independence Day or Poorna Swaraj Day.

questions.q: Which two laws were repealed by the Constitution when it became effective?
options: Government of India Act 1935 and the Constitution of India
Indian Independence Act 1947 and Government of India Act 1935
Poorna Swaraj resolution and the Declaration of Independence
Indian Independence Act 1947 and the Declaration of Independence
questions.explanation: The Constitution repealed the Indian Independence Act 1947 and the Government of India Act 1935.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Republic Day and Constitution Day fall on different dates.
Reason (R): The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on an earlier date than the day it came into effect.
options: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Adoption and coming into effect are different events on different dates, which is why the two observances differ.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Constitution adopted by the Constituent Assembly   ->   A. 26 November 1949
II. Constitution came into effect   ->   B. 26 January 1950
III. India gained independence   ->   C. 15 August 1947
IV. Lahore Session of INC passed the Poorna Swaraj resolution   ->   D. December 1929
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949, took effect on 26 January 1950, India gained independence on 15 August 1947, and the Poorna Swaraj resolution was passed in December 1929.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Republic Day:
I. India ceased to be a Dominion of the British Crown and became a Sovereign, Democratic Republic.
II. Republic Day is celebrated on 15 August each year.
III. Constitution Day is observed on 26 January each year.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since Republic Day is on 26 January and Constitution Day is on 26 November.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Congress urged Indians to celebrate 'Independence' on 26 January.
II. The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 January 1950.
III. India gained independence on 15 August 1947.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.

quizzes.title: Republic Day: History Recall
quizzes.passage: Republic Day is observed on 26 January, and its story is closely tied to India's freedom movement. A session of the Indian National Congress produced a resolution demanding total self-rule, sovereignty and complete independence from British rule. Congress then asked Indians to treat 26 January as a day of national pride, and the date was used in this way for many years. Freedom eventually arrived, and afterwards people reconsidered what the day should signify. The nation's legal framework was built through the work of the Constituent Assembly, which produced the Constitution of India. That Constitution replaced the earlier legal arrangements of colonial rule, so the country moved from being a Dominion of the Crown to a sovereign, democratic republic. Celebrations begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas in honour of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose's birth anniversary. Today the main celebrations take place at Kartavya Path, formerly Rajpath, in New Delhi, where a parade is held. The celebrations end with the Beating Retreat ceremony at Vijay Chowk. The 2026 parade showcased 30 cultural tableaux under the theme 150 Years of Vande Mataram. The parade showcased Constitutional values, and the day therefore recalls both the long struggle for freedom and the adoption of a constitutional system.

questions.q: In which city was the Indian National Congress session held that passed the Poorna Swaraj resolution in December 1929?
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies the Lahore Session of the INC as the session that passed the Poorna Swaraj resolution.

questions.q: What is the name of the resolution passed by the INC in December 1929 that demanded total self-rule and complete independence?
questions.explanation: The Poorna Swaraj resolution called for total self-rule, sovereignty and complete independence from British rule.

questions.q: In which year was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.

questions.q: Which Act of 1935 was repealed by the Constitution when it came into effect?
questions.explanation: The Constitution repealed the Government of India Act 1935 along with the Indian Independence Act 1947.

questions.q: In which year did India gain independence from British rule?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India gained independence on 15 August 1947.

questions.q: On which calendar day and month is Constitution Day observed?
questions.explanation: The booklet says 26 November is observed as Constitution Day.

questions.q: In which year did the Constitution come into effect?
questions.explanation: The Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950.

quizzes.title: Flag Unfurling and Hoisting
quizzes.passage: India observes two national days with the Tricolour, the National Flag, and each has its own ceremony. Republic Day falls on 26 January and marks the day the Constitution came into effect. Independence Day falls on 15 August and marks the nation's freedom from colonial rule. Although the flag is central to both occasions, the way it is handled differs between them. On Republic Day the flag is handled in a way that symbolically renews the nation's commitment to the principles of the Constitution. On Independence Day the flag is raised, a gesture with its own symbolism. The two ceremonies therefore carry different messages while sharing the same symbol. The main Republic Day parade is held at Kartavya Path, formerly known as Rajpath, in New Delhi, and the celebrations conclude with the Beating Retreat ceremony at Vijay Chowk on 29 January. Celebrations begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas in honour of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose's birth anniversary. The 2026 celebrations carried the theme 150 Years of Vande Mataram, and the parade featured 30 cultural tableaux. Republic Day festivities therefore run from 23 January to 29 January. Together these ceremonies remind citizens of the transition from colonial rule to a republic.

questions.q: Who unfurls the National Flag on Republic Day?
questions.explanation: The President, as Head of State, unfurls the Tricolour on 26 January.

questions.q: The hoisting of the National Flag on 15 August is said to symbolise:
options: Rise of a new nation, patriotism and freedom from colonial rule
Renewed commitment to the principles of the Constitution
Unveiling of the flag without pulling it up
Dominion status under the British Crown
questions.explanation: Hoisting symbolises the rise of a new nation, patriotism and freedom from colonial rule.

questions.q: Before the National Flag is raised on 15 August, where is it positioned on the pole?
options: Folded and attached to the top of the pole
Tied across the middle of the pole
At the bottom of the pole
questions.explanation: On 15 August the flag is positioned at the bottom of the pole and raised from bottom to top.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): On Republic Day the Tricolour is unfurled rather than hoisted.
Reason (R): On 26 January the flag is folded or rolled and attached to the top of the pole before it is unveiled.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The flag is attached at the top of the pole in folded form before unveiling, which is why it is unfurled rather than hoisted.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Republic Day (26 January)   ->   A. Tricolour is unfurled
II. Independence Day (15 August)   ->   B. Tricolour is hoisted
III. Head of State   ->   C. President
IV. Head of the Union Government   ->   D. Prime Minister
questions.explanation: Republic Day involves unfurling, Independence Day involves hoisting, the Head of State is the President and the Union Government is headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The President unveils the flag on 26 January without pulling it up.
II. On 15 August the flag is raised from top to bottom.
III. Unfurling highlights India's shift from a British colony to a Sovereign, Democratic Republic.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the flag is raised from bottom to top on 15 August.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The National Flag is hoisted on 26 January.
II. On 15 August the flag is raised from bottom to top.
III. The flag is unfurled on 15 August.
IV. The Prime Minister heads the Union Government.
questions.explanation: Statements II and IV are correct, while I and III are wrong because unfurling is done on 26 January and hoisting on 15 August.

quizzes.title: Flag Ceremony Recall
quizzes.passage: The Tricolour, India's National Flag, is central to two national occasions held each year. Republic Day is observed on 26 January, and Independence Day is observed on 15 August. Although the flag is present at both, each ceremony has its own character and its own meaning. The Republic Day ceremony recalls the moment when India's legal system took a new shape and the nation became a sovereign, democratic republic. The Independence Day ceremony marks the end of foreign rule and the arrival of freedom. Both occasions are linked to the flag. Celebrations begin on 23 January, observed as Parakram Divas in honour of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose's birth anniversary. Wreath-laying at Amar Jawan Jyoti takes place in the early morning of 26 January. The Republic Day parade is held at Kartavya Path, formerly Rajpath, in New Delhi, and the celebrations conclude on 29 January with the Beating Retreat at Vijay Chowk. The 2026 parade showcased 30 cultural tableaux under the theme 150 Years of Vande Mataram, and leading tableaux came from Maharashtra, Jammu and Kashmir, and Kerala. The address to the nation is delivered on the day before Republic Day. The 2026 celebration marks the 77th Republic Day, and the Beating Retreat marks the close of the celebrations.

questions.q: Who unfurls the National Flag on Republic Day? Give the office title.
questions.explanation: The President, as Head of State, unfurls the Tricolour on 26 January.

questions.q: Who hoists the National Flag on Independence Day? Give the office title.
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister, who heads the Union Government, hoists the flag on 15 August.

questions.q: On Republic Day, the folded or rolled flag is attached to which part of the pole? (one word)
questions.explanation: On 26 January the flag is folded or rolled and attached to the top of a pole.

questions.q: On Independence Day, the flag is raised from which end of the pole to which end?
questions.explanation: On 15 August the flag is positioned at the bottom of the pole and raised from bottom to top.

questions.q: Unfurling is a symbolic gesture to renew commitment to the principles of which document?
questions.explanation: Unfurling renews commitment to the principles laid down in the Constitution.

questions.q: Unfurling highlights India's shift from being a colony of which country?
questions.explanation: Unfurling highlights India's shift from being a British colony to a Sovereign, Democratic Republic.

questions.q: Hoisting the flag symbolises the rise of a what?
questions.explanation: Hoisting symbolises the rise of a new nation, patriotism and freedom from colonial rule.
